content.value_statement: Material pricing changes can affect revenue and customer retention without clear evidence or approval criteria. This workflow structures hypotheses, controlled tests, decision reviews, and post-rollout audits.
actual_capabilities: Classify pricing changes using revenue impact, affected customers, reversibility, and value-metric changes.
Develop hypotheses with expected outcomes, mechanisms, downside concentration, and falsification conditions.
Suggest controlled test formats, including private betas, sales pilots, cohorts, and phased rollouts.
Draft test plans with cohort selection, duration, kill-switch thresholds, and approval owners.
Apply a verdict matrix to supplied results and identify rollout, iteration, or abandonment outcomes.
Plan 30-, 60-, and 90-day reviews comparing actual outcomes with test predictions.
limitations: The skill provides planning guidance, not automated pricing changes or experiment execution.
Statistical significance, customer impacts, and revenue estimates require reliable data and independent analysis.
Calendar scheduling, approval requests, and monitoring need operator action or separate integrations.
The workflow references related pricing documents that are not included in this standalone skill.

use_cases.title: Review a Value-Metric Change
use_cases.description: Assess a move from flat subscription pricing to usage pricing, including customer downside and strategic approval requirements.

use_cases.title: Design a Sales Pricing Pilot
use_cases.description: Prepare a limited prospect pilot with predicted revenue changes, cohort criteria, and a documented stop condition.

use_cases.title: Audit a Pricing Rollout
use_cases.description: Compare post-launch results against predictions and document unexpected effects at 30-, 60-, and 90-day reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a Proposed Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pricing change: [change]. Estimated ARR impact: [percentage]; affected customers: [percentage]; reversal time: [days]. Identify the risk tier and missing information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: choose the appropriate review workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Pricing Hypothesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a hypothesis for [change]. Use these assumptions: [expected outcome, mechanism, and customer downside]. Include predicted magnitude, direction, and a falsification condition.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: make a proposed change testable.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tribunal test plan for [hypothesis] using [risk tier and available data]. Specify cohort, duration, kill-switch threshold, and approval owners. Mark unsupported assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a controlled pricing experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Adjudicate and Plan Follow-Up
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [test results] with [predictions] using the verdict matrix. Consider [side effects, downside concentration, and written approvals]. Recommend a verdict and post-rollout audit criteria. Identify inconclusive evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review evidence before a rollout decision.

output_examples.input: We propose usage-based pricing instead of a flat subscription. Revenue impact is estimated at 12%; reversal would take 90 days.
output: Risk tier: Strategic because the proposal changes the value metric and exceeds 10% estimated ARR impact.
Test window: 8-12 weeks, with executive review and grandfathering for existing customers.
Missing inputs: predicted lift, downside concentration, falsification condition, cohort size, and kill-switch threshold.

output_examples.input: We predicted a 20% ACV increase. The statistically significant result was 19%; side effects matched predictions and all owners approved in writing.
output: Direction: Pass. Magnitude: Pass because 19% is within the stated tolerance around the 20% prediction.
Side effects: Pass. Written approvals: Pass.
Downside concentration: Not supplied. Complete this check before declaring all criteria passed or recommending rollout.

output_examples.input: At the 30-day audit, churn exceeded our predicted downside after the pricing rollout.
output: Audit finding: Actual downside diverged from the test prediction.
Document the divergence reason in the failed-test registry.
Reassess side effects and customer concentration at the 60- and 90-day reviews.

best_practices: State expected magnitude, direction, mechanism, downside concentration, and falsification conditions before collecting results.
Record every changed input and document inconclusive tests instead of treating them as successful evidence.
Name approval owners, define stop thresholds, and confirm review dates with the operator.
anti_patterns: Treating a full pricing cutover as a controlled experiment.
Changing multiple inputs without documenting attribution limits.
Approving rollout without complete evidence, written sign-offs, or post-rollout review dates.

faq.question: What does Pricing Tribunal produce?
faq.answer: It drafts a pricing plan with a hypothesis, test design, approval owners, adjudication date, and post-rollout review dates.

faq.question: When should I use the full workflow?
faq.answer: Use it for material or strategic changes involving revenue impact, affected customers, limited reversibility, or a new value metric.

faq.question: Does it run experiments or change live prices?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and planning templates. Operators must execute experiments and manage pricing changes.

faq.question: Does it calculate statistical significance?
faq.answer: No statistical calculation method is included. Provide validated results or identify the test as inconclusive.

faq.question: Can I invoke it directly as a command?
faq.answer: Its metadata marks it as not user-invocable. The main pricing skill normally routes relevant decisions to this workflow.

faq.question: Does it schedule audits and send approvals?
faq.answer: No calendar or messaging integration is included. It asks the operator to confirm scheduling, approval requests, and monitoring.
